thread.title: Fitbit Stock Is Falling and Apple’s to Blame

author: David Marino-Nachison
title: Fitbit Stock Is Falling and Apple’s to Blame
text:
Photo: Apple By David Marino-Nachison Sept. 12, 2018 2:30 p.m. ET You could almost feel it coming: The more Apple (AAPL) talked about health technology during Wednesday’s event — during which it discussed updates to both the Apple Watch and the iPhone — the more likely it was that Fitbit stock was due for a slide.
Sure enough, it happened: The company’s shares were recently off about 5%, while Apple’s were down roughly 1%. (Both companies are Barron’s Next 50 stocks.)
Newsletter Sign-up You don’t need to look too far back in the timeline to understand why. Last month, Fitbit announced its latest fitness tracker, the Charge 3 , highlighting a number of heath-related features—as well as plans to keep developing more. Sleep apnea and atrial fillibration (or, put more simply, irregular heartbeat) were among the conditions it said it would “ continue to develop and clinically validate ” features for.
Apple, meanwhile, made health a centerpiece of its Apple Watch 4 announcement: It highlighted features including fall detection and heart rate monitoring, among other features . The watch, Apple COO Jeff Williams said in a press release, now “becomes an intelligent guardian for your health.”
Fitbit, shares of which are currently down about 2%in 2018, wants to distinguish itself as a company that can offer compelling health apps—in both watch and tracker form—that could be attractive to consumers, but also potentially employers and health care companies looking to tweak consumer behavior.
More About Barron’s Next Learn more about Barron’s Next The Barron’s Next 50 Some recent product launches have been well-received , with the company having managed to sustain its brand as the Apple Watch led a rapid evolution of the wearables category away from the fitness bands on which it made its name. In the latest quarter, according to IDC data , the company came third worldwide in wearables shipments. (Apple was first.)
A few specific launches are, naturally, just part of the bigger story. In that sense, it’s likely that the Fitbit investor reaction to today’s Apple news might have been overdramatic. If nothing else, it’s a reminder that Fitbit has some big-time competition that sees just as much opportunity as it does.
